title: Time series change points
text: mcp implements AR MA generalized ARMA (GARMA) recurrence response-family link scale. b_t ordinary regression predictor segment formulas \eta_t predictor including serial dependence, \begin{aligned} \text{AR}_t &= \sum_{j=1}^{p} \phi_{j,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-j}) - b_{t-j}\right] \\ \text{MA}_t &= \sum_{k=1}^{q} \theta_{k,t} \left[g(y^*_{t-k}) - \eta_{t-k}\right] \\ \eta_t &= b_t + \text{AR}_t + \text{MA}_t \end{aligned} \phi_{j,t} lag-j autoregressive (AR) coefficient time t, \theta_{k,t} lag-k moving-average (MA) coefficient time t, g(\cdot) link function, y^* boundary-constrained observation. Thus ar() uses lagged link-scale residuals relative ordinary regression, ma() uses lagged one-step innovations. mcp regression change points coefficients \phi_{j,t} \theta_{k,t}. See applied examples. GARMA currently supports default links gaussian() (identity), binomial() (logit), bernoulli() (logit), poisson() (log), negbinomial() (log). Non-default links rejected now. title: Understanding mcp formulas
text: three formula parts called response, cp, predictor. general format response ~ cp ~ predictor, except first segment, change point therefore uses response ~ predictor. later segments response inherited may omitted. one-sided formula ~ x also uses default change-point formula ~ 1, shorthand y ~ 1 ~ 1 + x. familiar lm()/glm()/brms::brm(). mcp model consist three parts: response part defined segment 1. E.g. y ~ ... y | weights(w) ~ ... y | trials(N) + weights(w) ~ ... binomial models, etc.. “cp” part specifies change point modeling. can 1 ~ ... population-level 1 + (1|group) ~ ... group-level (random) change-point deviations. predictor part regular ~ 1 + x 0 + x:condition + z + (1|id). regression models can also applied distributional parameters using + sigma(1 + x) shape(0 + condition) (read ). applies time-series ar(1) intercept first-order autogregression ma(2, 1 + x) second-order MA regression (read ). mcp heavily inspired brms inspired lme4::lmer() extends lm() glm(). bit history .

title: Understanding mcp formulas
text: Mathematically, mcp model divides continuous predictor x K segments separated ordered change points \Delta_1 < \dots < \Delta_{K-1}. segment k \\{1, \dots, K\}, linear predictor \mu_i (\eta_i) evaluated directly segment-local distance (x_i - \Delta_{k-1}): \mu_i = \alpha_k + \beta_{k,1} \, (x_i - \Delta_{k-1}) \quad (\text{} \Delta_0 = 0) segment-start level \alpha_k freely estimated first disjoined segments, non-segmented regression, inherited continuously joined segments: \alpha_k = \begin{cases} \beta_{k,0}, & \text{Disjoined segments } (\sim \texttt{1 + x}, \text{ including } k = 1) \\ \alpha_{k-1} + \beta_{k-1,1} (\Delta_{k-1} - \Delta_{k-2}), & \text{Joined segments } (k \ge 2, \, \sim \texttt{0 + x}) \end{cases} segments, estimated slope intercept parameters absolute values (changes relative preceding segments).

title: Understanding mcp formulas
text: Bayesian MCMC samplers like JAGS evaluate dynamic conditional statements (/else) parameters sampled. implement piecewise model JAGS, mcp uses indicator plateauing formulation (evaluated via Iverson brackets [] equal 1 true 0 false). First, mcp defines segment-local span X_{k,} grows linearly within segment k “freezes” (plateaus) segment boundary: X_{1,} = \min(x_i, \Delta_1) X_{k,} = \max\bigl(0, \min(x_i, \Delta_k) - \Delta_{k-1}\bigr) \quad (k \ge 2) x_i < \Delta_{k-1}, X_{k,} = 0 (inactive). \Delta_{k-1} \le x_i < \Delta_k, X_{k,} = x_i - \Delta_{k-1} (linear growth). x_i \ge \Delta_k, X_{k,} = \Delta_k - \Delta_{k-1} (frozen segment width). purely joined model (list(y ~ 0 + x, ~ 0 + x)), mcp writes \mu_i cumulative sum plateauing coordinates: \mu_i = \sum_{k=1}^K [x_i \ge \Delta_{k-1}] \cdot \beta_{k,1} X_{k,} earlier segments freeze boundary levels (\beta_{k-1,1}(\Delta_{k-1} - \Delta_{k-2})), continuity automatic zero parameter constraints: preceding segments hand flat plateau serves baseline subsequent segments. segment disjoined (~ 1 + x), introduces new explicit intercept \beta_{k,0} \Delta_{k-1}, earlier terms capped [x_i < \Delta_{\text{next}}] previous segments stop accumulating. title: Working with priors
text: Change point locations must lie within observed range [min(x), max(x)] maintain strict order cp_1 < cp_2 < ... < cp_n. Without rule, change point locations unidentifiable label switching occur. default prior change points mcp uniform order statistics (dirichlet(1)), treats set ordered change points equally likely anywhere observed interval [min(x), max(x)]. See visualization. properties prior: Single change point: 1 change point, reduces uniform prior observed range: \text{cp}_1 \sim \text{Beta}(1, 1) \equiv \text{Uniform}(\min(x), \max(x)). Multiple change points: N \ge 2, change points evenly spaced average: \mathbb{E}[\text{cp}_j] = \min(x) + \frac{j}{N + 1} (\max(x) - \min(x)) example, 2 change points, prior means 33% 67% data range. 5 change points, 16.7%, 33.3%, 50%, 66.7%, 83.3%. Symmetry flat sum: prior symmetric reflection (flipping x leaves prior probabilities unchanged), sum prior densities across change points uniform across entire data range. Increasing informativeness segment count: given range, introducing change points makes prior change point effectively informative “squeezed” together (shown figure ). plot compares theoretical Dirichlet distributions (black lines) sampled prior distributions (red lines) 2 5 change points:  Note implementation: hood, mcp parameterizes using sequential stick-breaking Beta chain (z_j \sim \text{Beta}(1, N - j + 1), \text{cp}_j = \text{cp}_{j-1} + z_j(\max(x) - \text{cp}_{j-1})). allows JAGS sample model much efficiently. Dirichlet distribution places joint prior positive segment spacings sum observed x-range. construction also underlies monotonic effects brms (Bürkner & Charpentier (2019)).

code: fit_manual$jags_code ## model { ##   # mcp helper values ##   cp_0 = CONST1_ ##   cp_3 = CONST2_ ##  ##   # Priors for population-level effects ##   cp_1 ~ dunif(CONST1_, cp_2)  # User-specified prior ##   cp_2 = CONST3_  # Fixed at 80 ##   Intercept_1 ~ dnorm(0, 1/(5)^2) T(,10)  # User-specified prior ##   x_1 ~ dbeta(2, 5)  # User-specified prior ##   Intercept_2 ~ dt(26, 1/(10.3)^2, 3)   # Robustly centered mean intercept with a minimum scale of 2.5 ##   x_2 ~ dt(0, 1/(1)^2, 3) T(x_1,)  # User-specified prior ##   Intercept_3 ~ dt(26, 1/(10.3)^2, 3)   # Robustly centered mean intercept with a minimum scale of 2.5 ##   x_3 = x_2  # Same value as x_2 ##   sigma_1 ~ dt(0, 1/(10.3)^2, 3) T(0.001,)  # Positive residual SD calibrated on the response scale ##  ##   # Model and likelihood ##   for (i_ in 1:length(x)) { ##     # par_x local to each segment ##     x_local_1_[i_] = min(x[i_], cp_1) ##     x_local_2_[i_] = min(x[i_], cp_2) - cp_1 ##     x_local_3_[i_] = min(x[i_], cp_3) - cp_2 ##      ##     # Formula for mu ##     link_mu_[i_] = ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * (x[i_] < cp_1) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(1)], c(Intercept_1)) * 1 +  ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * (x[i_] < cp_1) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(2)], c(x_1)) * x_local_1_[i_] +  ##       (x[i_] >= cp_1) * (x[i_] < cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(3)], c(Intercept_2)) * 1 +  ##       (x[i_] >= cp_1) * (x[i_] < cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(4)], c(x_2)) * x_local_2_[i_] +  ##       (x[i_] >= cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(5)], c(Intercept_3)) * 1 +  ##       (x[i_] >= cp_2) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(6)], c(x_3)) * x_local_3_[i_] ##      ##     # Formula for sigma ##     link_sigma_[i_] = ##       (x[i_] >= cp_0) * inprod(rhs_matrix_[i_, c(7)], c(sigma_1)) * 1 ##  ##     # Likelihood and log-density for family = gaussian() ##     mu_[i_] = link_mu_[i_] ##     sigma_[i_] = max(1e-03, link_sigma_[i_]) ##     y[i_] ~ dnorm(mu_[i_], 1 / sigma_[i_]^2) ##   } ## }

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: Multiple regression: mcp now supports several continuous predictors, categorical predictors, interactions, etc. terms RHS. E.g., ~ 1 + x + x:group + sigma(1 + group) + ar(2, 0 + z). Basically, now aims “feels” like lm() glm() distributional parameter segment. Explore ex = mcp_example("multiple") see action. Default priors generally align brms, adjustments accommodate change-point model. Group-level effects RHS: Predictor formulas now support group-level effects (random effects) using familiar lme4 brms syntax. (1 | group) specifies group-level intercept, (1 + x || group) (factor || group) support independent coefficients, including slopes factors. also works inside distributional formulas sigma(1 + (factor || id)). ar(), effect carries later segments redefined disabled (0 | group). See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. Correlated multi-coefficient terms yet supported. Native feel: mcpfits now work natively R generics, posterior tidybayes posterior draw prediction API. Changes include: summary(fit) now reports rank-normalized split-rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail posterior central quantile intervals instead HDIs. Adding as_draws(fit), as_draws_df(fit), tidy_draws(fit), ndraws(fit), rstantools linpred/epred, etc. full S3 generic registration posterior, rstantools, tidybayes (spread_draws(), gather_draws()). Per-draw methods (summary = FALSE fitted(), predict(), residuals(), log_lik()) now return dot-prefixed columns (.epred, .prediction, .residual, .loglik) tidybayes / ggdist compatibility. nsamples soft-deprecated favor ndraws; which_y deprecated favor dpar. Added R generics mcpfits: formula(fit), family(fit), model.frame(fit), nobs(fit), vcov(fit), confint(fit). Fits now also store proper matched $call. Printed summaries now report posterior sd new layout. Negative binomial offset(): can now mcp(..., family = negbinomial()). NB (Poisson) can now model rates exposure offset() now supported formulas - also families. Dirichlet now default prior change points: default change point prior now mathematically beautiful principled dirichlet(1) (flat Dirichlet / uniform order statistics). Effectively, prior remain unchanged models 1 change point Dirichlet reduces uniform prior. models 2+ change points, previous “truncated-t” prior removed. served purpose higher ESS/s expense mathematically unprincipled. previous mcp versions supported slow implementation Dirichlet, achieving good ESS/s made possible parameterizing dirichlet sequential stick-breaking Beta chain (z_j \sim \text{Beta}(1, N - j + 1)). Comparing mcp_example(), estimates remain essentially identical truncated-t dirichlet. hypothesis(fit, "cp_1 = 20") (Savage-Dickey Bayes Factor) default priors likely differ, BF ill advised default priors anyway - hypothesis() throws warning attempted. Read mcp website. Missing response imputation: Missing responses now retained posterior JAGS imputations. predict(fit) |> filter(.na(y)) can used see imputed values - similarly fitted(). supports AR/MA . Missing values AR/MA supported log_lik(), loo(), waic() throw informative error. See details new vignette/article missing data.

title: mcp 0.4.0
text: mcp v0.4 major breaking change aim remaining relatively stable going forward towards version 1.0. Although lot updated, parameter estimates v0.4.0 remain practically identical previous public release (v0.3.4). Deprecation detections added reach 1.0. Renaming align brms posterior: Renamed parameters consistent brms: int_i –> Intercept_i; x_1_E2 –> xE2_1; x_1_sin –> sinx_1, etc. summary(), fixef(), ranef() now name parameter identifier column variable instead name, directly matching posterior posterior::summarise_draws(). fitted(), predict(), residuals(), pp_eval() summary = TRUE now return sd instead error posterior standard deviation (posterior predictive standard deviation), avoiding ambiguity data column collisions. Rhat renamed rhat summary(), fixef(), ranef(), match posterior standard. hypothesis() returns column prob instead p posterior (prior) probability directional hypotheses, preventing confusion frequentist p-values. summary(), fixef(), ranef(), prior_summary(), everything else now return rows canonical order instead previous incidental (near-alphabetical) order. Use verbose = TRUE summary(), fixef(), ranef() include segment dpar columns. plot() now split plot() plotting full fits plot_dpar() plots one distributional parameter (mu, sigma, shape, ar1, etc.). argument order changed . new coloring function (plot(fit, color_by = "column")) particularly useful models include categorical predictors rhs group-level effects. See mcp_example("group_mu") worked example. hypothesis() now restricts equality tests simple parameter contrasts gives clearer guidance Savage-Dickey Bayes factors. Non-linear transformations hypotheses like x_1 / x_2 = 1 previously run, even though Savage-Dickey support . Equality tests now return prob = NA Bayes factor model comparison, posterior parameter probability. Density estimates robust, warn evaluating Savage-Dickey Bayes factors default priors, warn sparse tails. fixef() now reports population-level effects mu (primary response parameter), excluding change points, distributional parameters, AR/MA parameters, group-effect SDs. Use summary(fit) get parameters. fit$pars removed. Use mcp_pars(fit) canonical table model parameters mcp_columns(fit) resolved data-column roles, including automatically chosen par_x. general, renamed "varying" "group". old "varying" selector remains deprecated alias. established varying = method argument remains unchanged now. y | weights(w) now specifies observation log-likelihood weights across supported families (gaussian(), binomial(), bernoulli(), poisson(), negbinomial()), rather Gaussian-precision weights (previously scaled residual SD sigma / sqrt(w)). Unlike brms, weights must strictly positive due JAGS requirements. Predictive draws expectations now use distribution parameters directly log_lik() multiplies observation log-densities w. AR MA intercepts now zero-centered, regularizing dnorm(0, 0.5) T(-1, 1) priors, replacing independent uniform priors. categorical contrasts numeric slopes now use modest normal priors instead heavy-tailed Student-t priors. Coefficients remain direct jointly constrained stationary invertible regions. Gaussian models explicit sigma() formula now model residual standard deviation log link, brms. Models without explicit sigma() unchanged: sigma_1 remains residual SD response-scale half-Student-t prior. Formula transformations now use original predictor values, lm(), glm(), brms. Previously, transformations change-point predictor sin(x) exp(x) restarted segment onset. Bare par_x polynomial bases (par_x^2) remain segment-local support joined segment shapes. Corrected JAGS translation prior scales. ddexp() dlogis() now convert conventional scale inverse scale rather inverse variance; exported sd_to_prec() helper soft-deprecated prior translation now internal, sampler-specific step. Group-level change points (1|id) now use standard hierarchical normal model sampled efficiently absolute locations. makes cp_i_sd latent normal scale rather realized sample SD. sampling, mcp() now verifies population- group-level change points strictly ordered every draw realized change points lie within observed predictor range. ordering broken, wrong segments apply. Parallel sampling now controlled exclusively active future plan. cores argument mcp() deprecated ignored, remains available backwards compatibility. Use future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 3) calling mcp() sample chains parallel, future::plan(future::sequential) shut workers. Without parallel future plan, chains sampled sequentially. mcp(..., adapt = 1000) soft-deprecated favor mcp(..., warmup = 1000) compatibility additional future samplers. Dropped support rel() formulas. ambiguous interaction terms made code hard maintain. Another way achieving functionality via priors may added future versions. arguments fit$simulate() changed accommodate multiple (categorical) predictors. fit$simulate(fit, data, ..., .type = "predict") new argument structure. Note (1) now requires fit first argument, (2) requires data.frame tibble second argument instead just vector par_x, (3) arguments prefixed “.” avoid name conflicts internally mcp. ... model parameters usual. Dropped support mcp(..., data = NULL). now must provide mock-data inform mcp types levels predictor columns. See, e.g., mcp_example("intercepts")$example_code simple example mcp_example("multiple")$example_code involved example. docs updated appropriately. mcp longer exports phi, logit, ilogit, probit.

Default plot(fit) style updated many ways accommodate multiple regression group-effects. Predictive intervals (plot(fit, q_predict = TRUE) predict(fit, summary = TRUE)) now precise faster. used estimated posterior parameter draws, MC error. Added log_lik(fit) returns draws--observation matrix default. usual brms return shape accepted directly loo. log_lik() supports arguments e.g. fitted(). Partial lists override defaults, individual diagnostics can disabled NULL, diagnostics = FALSE disables diagnostic warnings. summary(fit) inherits settings accepts override diagnostic footer. Added AR/MA warnings: (1) AR/MA models loo(), predict(), etc. serial dependence currently ignored. Proper handling requires leave-future-blocked cross-validation, currently implemented mcp. (2) posterior violation probabilities exceed configurable ar ma diagnostic thresholds (10% default). Several new arguments loo. loo(fit, pointwise = TRUE) uses loo::loo.function() memory-efficient (slower) computation LOO. new arguments include usual fitted() etc.: loo(fit, ndraws = 1000, arma = FALSE, varying = FALSE). Added interpolate_newdata(fit, = NULL) generates data.frame combinations categorical predictors along interpolated continuous predictors. Use include grouping factors. documentation shows can useful generating custom plots simple tweaking plot() enough. Fits made custom jags_code now warn calling R-side simulation, prediction, model-evaluation methods, methods continue evaluate supplied formulas rather custom JAGS code.
